title: Closest Room
summary: Given a hotel with unique numbered rooms and their sizes, and a set of k queries each specifying a preferred room number and a minimum size requirement, find the room number that meets the size requirement and has the smallest absolute difference with the preferred room number.
statement: Given a hotel with unique numbered rooms and their sizes, and a set of k queries each specifying a preferred room number and a minimum size requirement, find the room number that meets the size requirement and has the smallest absolute difference with the preferred room number. If there are multiple rooms with the same smallest absolute difference, choose the room with the smallest room number. If no room meets the criteria, return -1 for that query. Return an array containing the answers to all queries.
constraints: Room IDs are unique; each query is [preferred_id,minimum_size].
Choose an eligible room minimizing absolute ID difference, breaking ties by smaller ID; return -1 if none.
hints: Process queries from largest minimum size downward and activate rooms as they become eligible.
Coordinate-compress room IDs and store active positions in a Fenwick tree.
For each preferred ID, obtain the active predecessor and successor by prefix counts and order-statistic lookup.
Only the nearest active ID on each side can win; offline activation enforces size eligibility and the final tuple comparison enforces distance and tie rules.
editorial: Only the nearest active ID on each side can win; offline activation enforces size eligibility and the final tuple comparison enforces distance and tie rules.

tests.explanation: The answers are room three, no room, and room three.
Rooms one and three tie for the first query, so smaller room one wins; the second has no eligible room.
